record.summary: A 289-bed, six-story integrated hospital complex at 1975 4th St combining UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital, UCSF Bakar Cancer Hospital and Betty Irene Moore Women's Hospital under one roof, which opened February 1, 2015 after over a decade of planning, design and construction.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is the union of Assessor lots 8723008, 3992003, 8724001 and 8729001 (59,505 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed building footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lot and can sit a little off the walls. Until 2026-10-12 this record showed the surveyed building footprint (OpenStreetMap (way 580277612, name=UCSF Medical Center at Mission Bay, amenity=hospital, operator=University of California San Francisco, 1975 4th St)); 94% of that outline lies inside the lot and it covered 93% of the lot. The outline has two parts because lot 8723008 (601 16th St) does not touch the others. That these four lots are the hospital's own is Pier & Point's inference from location, shape and size (each lies at least 90% inside the earlier outline); no source read ties the lot numbers to the hospital. Four other lots lie mostly inside the earlier outline and are left out, because nothing read ties them to it: 8728001 (770 Mariposa St) and 3943001, 3943003 and 3943007 (1800 and 1830 3rd St). Other UCSF buildings in Mission Bay stay on their building footprints because several buildings share one large lot (for example blklot 8711507, about 12 acres).
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lots 8723008, 3992003, 8724001 and 8729001 (mapped 1998-07-01, 2001-03-20, 2006-05-24; active), joined into one outline; the earlier outline came from: OpenStreetMap (way 580277612, name=UCSF Medical Center at Mission Bay, amenity=hospital, operator=University of California San Francisco, 1975 4th St)

facts.value: Stantec (formerly Anshen+Allen) and William McDonough + Partners are both credited as architects on McDonough's project page; DPR's project page credits Stantec Architecture

costs.what: Project value as stated by the general contractor, DPR Construction ("the ground-up, $1.52 billion UCSF Medical Center at Mission Bay"); a contractor's headline figure, not a final audited cost. The UC Regents' September 2008 presentation gave a different total, a $1.686 billion project budget (slide 27, "Project Cost Breakdown"), which is a pre-construction approved budget, not a final cost; the two are not reconciled

milestones.text: UC Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings certifies the project EIR and approves LRDP Amendment #3 for the UCSF Medical Center at Mission Bay; a February 2009 Regents item recounts that "on September 17, 2008, the Regents certified the UCSF Medical Center at Mission Bay EIR and approved LRDP Amendment #3". The same meeting's budget item (J1, September 17, 2008) and the staff presentation asked the Regents to approve the design, the $1.686 billion project budget and the financing ("Today: Request Regents approval of design, EIR and project budget"); no source read reports the outcome of the design, site-plan or budget requests. The presentation concerns this hospital specifically, per its site plan (Attachment, p.15) laying out the hospital buildings, parking and phase boundary

open_questions: UCSF's own official press-kit page and several ucsf.edu archive pages could not be checked directly; the figures above come from a UCSF news post plus the contractor's own project page, not the hospital's own current fact sheet.
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.

The UCSF news post (2014-11) cited for the opening, the $1.5 billion cost and the hospital's use could not be checked as of September 2026; DPR's project page (read) states the $1.52 billion cost, the 289-bed, six-story, 878,000 sq ft facility and the February 1, 2015 opening, and McDonough's page lists 'Children, women's, and cancer hospitals'. The earlier '10 years of planning and 5 years of construction' split appears only in the UCSF release, which could not be checked; DPR says 'over a decade of planning, design and construction'.

Update 2026-10-12, cost: $1.52 billion is the contractor DPR's stated project value, and the only total in a readable source that describes the finished hospital. The UC Regents' September 2008 presentation (slide 27) shows a $1.686 billion project cost breakdown (construction $1,094.9 million; equipment and furnishings $239 million; special items and capitalized interest $174.6 million; contingency $54.7 million; design fees $70 million; project management $30 million; surveys, tests, plans and specifications $22.8 million) and slide 28 the same total as funding sources. The difference between a contractor's project value and a 2008 approved budget is not reconciled, and UCSF's own November 2014 release could not be read (access refused). The opening date of February 1, 2015 is from DPR's project page.
